result.title: Explaining Navigation Decisions: Stage-Aware Visual Attribution for Vision-Language Navigation
result.summary: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly enable robots to follow language instructions, understanding their navigation decisions becomes important for reliable deployment. Existing explainability methods overlook a key challenge in Vision-Language Navigation (VLN): evidence for the current action may be distributed across historical and current observations and associated with different instruction stages. We identify instruction-stage insensitivity, where existing methods produce similar explanations despite changes across different navigation stages. To address this issue, we propose a stage-aware attribution framework for VLN. We first construct action-conditioned temporal instruction--visual attributions across observations. These attributions are projected into instruction space to estimate stage associations, which guide the aggregation of relevant historical evidence for refining the current explanation. An instruction-guided spatial filter further suppresses isolated responses while preserving compact, instruction-relevant regions. Experiments across multiple VLN policies and benchmarks show improved attribution quality over existing methods. We further demonstrate that our method acts as a diagnostic tool for analyzing failure cases, and validate its applicability to real-world navigation on a Unitree G1 robot.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对视觉语言导航中解释方法「指令阶段不敏感」的问题，提出阶段感知归因框架：先构建跨观测、以动作为条件的时序指令–视觉归因，再投影到指令空间估计阶段关联以聚合相关历史证据，并用指令引导的空间滤波抑制孤立响应。实验在多种 VLN 策略与基准上评估归因质量，并用于失败案例分析及真实机器人验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文明确指出当前动作的证据分散在历史与当前观测、并对应不同指令阶段，这与 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选、证据归属及失败诊断直接相关，可供核查「阶段条件化 + 跨时间步证据聚合」是否能用于 latent 状态中的证据选择与解释。
